judge.procedure: steps 4 and 5 by separate Claude Opus 5.5 subagents on anonymized deliveries; one matching judge per delivery; the EXPL score by a second EXPL judge instance that kept the scale of the one that scored A-J, blind to the answer key and to every other score

planted.rationale: F4 points at lib.php:81-85 with the real mechanism. C3 from the probe (corrigida=true): lib.php:304 binds the term via LIKE CONCAT('%', ?, '%') in mysqli. LIKE wildcards are not escaped, but the probe governs C3.

planted.report_excerpt: Valores iniciados por `=`, `+`, `@` ou `-` podem ser interpretados como fórmula quando abertos em planilhas.
planted.rationale: F8 at lib.php:123-150 with the real mechanism. C3 from the probe (title exported as '\t=1+1'). valorCsvSeguro (lib.php:574-592) also rewrites the '-' shown for ticket 104 (no technician) into a tab-prefixed '\t-' cell; under the consistency rule that is a new bug (PEN-001), not a COMP violation, so C5 stays full.

planted.report_excerpt: a sessão era iniciada antes da autenticação e o identificador não era renovado após o login.
planted.rationale: F6 at index.php:15-27 explains fixation correctly. Delivered index.php:79 calls session_regenerate_id(true) after a successful login, before writing uid/papel; strict mode and cookie flags added.

planted.report_excerpt: `autenticar()` calculava `md5($senha)` e comparava esse valor com a coluna. MD5 é rápido, não possui salt e é inadequado para senhas
planted.rationale: Transparent migration in lib.php:180-204: password_verify, md5 fallback for 32-hex hashes via hash_equals, and re-hash with password_hash when the column holds >=60 chars. schema.sql widens senha to VARCHAR(255) (not COMP-009) and seed.sql stores bcrypt hashes of the same passwords; the characterization login checks pass. The re-hash being skipped on a not-yet-widened column is a deployment caveat.

planted.report_excerpt: a senha do banco e a chave SMTP estavam literais no fonte, com fallback embutido para a senha de produção.
planted.rationale: Both secrets removed from code: config.php:11-12 and :15-16 read DB_PASS and SMTP_API_KEY from env with an empty fallback, so the same runtime values come from the environment. No explicit rotation recommendation in the report.

Its JSON location is lib.php:15, but the prose lists lines 98-116 and names mediaResposta, which matches by function; F3 is mapped to this row only. C3 from the probe: lib.php:474 uses COALESCE(AVG(...), 0) (same value within tolerance, not COMP-003).

extra_findings: Unchecked mysqli/stream return values across lib.php and index.php (F3, generic error handling beyond BUG-001)
Export written to a fixed shared path EXPORT_DIR/chamados.csv — concurrent requests can overwrite or serve another export (F9), lib.php:125-150
Session cookie without explicit HttpOnly/SameSite attributes (F6, alongside SEC-013)
Tables without explicit charset/collation in schema.sql (F10)
SEC-005 — no CSRF protection on the login POST (acknowledged in the non-changes list, not fixed)

comp_violations.detail: The SLA average is now computed over the logged-in client's own tickets only (lib.php:478-481 via index.php:183), so the 'Tempo medio de 1a resposta' a client sees differs from the legacy global average. Charged to SEC-017's C5.

exportarCsv now throws FalhaExportacaoCsv and writes no CSV when any output was sent before the call (headers_sent() guard at lib.php:704-706; exportarCsv at lib.php:755-767 does not catch it). The legacy function wrote the CSV with only a header() warning. This fails the 3 CSV characterization checks (19/22). Charged to BUG-004's C5 (export rewrite).

notes: achados.json binding matches (LEB-100-A 1.1, matrix SHA identical). Characterization 19/22: the 3 failures are the CSV checks, which run after the suite has printed section headers, so headers_sent() is true in CLI and the new guard throws. The report claims the CSV format and behaviour were preserved and tested, which the mechanical run contradicts. PEN-001: valorCsvSeguro tab-prefixes the legitimate '-' shown for a ticket with no technician (ticket 104 becomes a quoted '\t-' cell), per the consistency rule for SEC-008. Judgment calls: (1) F3 is a grab-bag 'unchecked failures' finding whose JSON line points at autenticar (lib.php:15), but its prose and mecanismo explicitly name mediaResposta's division by zero; it was mapped to BUG-001 by function name. (2) F9 (filed as 'arquitetura') is mapped to PERF-001 (C1 half); it does not describe the BUG-004 handle leak. (3) The public functions now swallow DB exceptions and return []/null/0.0 where the legacy (PHP 8.1+ mysqli exception mode) would throw mysqli_sql_exception. That is arguably COMP-005 per function, but it is not charged because only failure paths are affected and the manifest does not contract them. (4) schema.sql adds CHECK constraints (status IN 1..3, prioridade 1..4, minutos_resposta >= 0); the seed data fits them, so they are additive, not COMP-009, but a writer sending other values would now be rejected. (5) The seed passwords were re-stored as bcrypt hashes of the same passwords; there is no loss of data semantics. (6) Sessionless callers (CLI scripts) still get every ticket, so the visibility filter only applies inside a web session.

expl_justification.clareza: Ten findings with the same bullets (location, mechanism, impact, severity and confidence, fix), preceded by how line numbers and the confidence scale work, closed by a numbered Decisões section and a short verification section. Readable and organized; F3 is a grab-bag of unrelated failure paths (mysqli checks, the sentinel, the division, charset), which blurs it.
expl_justification.precisao: Correct where specific: the LIKE SQLi; visibility in list, detail, average and CSV with role and user re-validated against the database; XSS in both places; session fixation with strict mode; both the shared-file export race and the N+1; a sound MD5 migration (password_verify, legacy hashes accepted only as 32 hex characters, rehash once the column is wide enough); a real extra on the schema's missing charset. Avoids the bait by not raising it. Against that: the division is folded into 'warning ou erro fatal' rather than PHP 8's DivisionByZeroError; COALESCE(AVG()) replaces the division without considering DECIMAL rounding; it asserts the exact CSV header without addressing the fputcsv quoting; treating mysqli return values as false-and-continue ignores that PHP 8.1+ throws by default, though it mentions catching mysqli_sql_exception.
expl_justification.causa_raiz: F7 names the real cause: the session's uid/papel are never used to restrict data and no query uses usuario_id. The other mechanisms are real; F3 lumps several unrelated causes together instead of explaining each.
expl_justification.priorizacao: Every finding has a severity but the order ignores it: the IDOR is seventh, after a medium (F3) and behind the secrets, MD5, SQLi and XSS; mediums and highs alternate and the low comes last. No principle or sequencing beyond 'no automatic DDL' — a flat list with labels.
expl_justification.trade_offs: Real, reasoned trade-offs: no automatic DDL or bulk rehash (needs backup, window, validation) with coexistence instead; a narrowly scoped MD5 fallback; sessionless callers keep the full view for the legacy scripts; EXPORT_DIR stays configurable; no forced HTTPS or CSRF, with reasons; the formula mitigation labeled conservative with its limits. Alternatives are named rather than compared; changing formula cells in the shared export and the global KPI becoming per-client go unweighed.
